post_result_generator_scale_diagnostic.interpretation: The relative within-landscape q70 traversability rule produces a much tighter absolute environmental edge tolerance after smoothing. The G2 reversal therefore exposes sensitivity to how environmental continuity is operationalized, not simply an autocorrelation main effect.

interpretation: Barriers strongly and monotonically increased the fraction of locally permissive nodes that were unreachable.
Sparse rook neighbourhoods created more critical stepping-stone dependence, while queen neighbourhoods increased single-node route robustness.
Static source-history ambiguity was large: the median alias count was 21.
Time-stamped positive constraints strongly contracted source-history ambiguity, with median contraction 0.815 among eligible rows.
Unreachable targets had heterogeneous minimal rescue mechanisms: barrier-only, environment-only, either-axis, jointly-required, and non-edge-rescuable cases all occurred.
The sole preregistered directional refutation, G2, reveals that an analyst's relative environmental-threshold rule can reverse an intuitive autocorrelation expectation.
claim_boundary: Frequencies are properties of the frozen generator, not nature.
The post-result G2 scale diagnostic does not repair or reclassify G2; G2 remains REFUTED.
